name: Elk Fork Campground
note: Shoshone NF, Wapiti Ranger District: a small campground strung along a gravel road beside Elk Fork creek just south of US-14/16/20, about 28 mi W of Cody, at the Elk Fork Trailhead into the Washakie Wilderness. The horse corrals and trailer lots belong to the trailhead beyond the back of the campground, not to the sites; the sites themselves are small with little room to manoeuvre, and the big lot at the back is the place to turn around. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Shoshone NF page fs.usda.gov/r02/shoshone/recreation/elk-fork-campground (read 2026-11-20, 'Site Open', last updated 2025-03-10): 'This campground hosts 13 sites ... Corrals are provided at the trailhead.'; 'Notes: Horse corrals and trailer parking are available. Maximum spur 22 feet.'; $15/night single unit; no reservations (FS EDW recreation layer reservation_info 'No'; not on recreation.gov, search 2026-11-20). Esri imagery 2026-11-20: a gravel camp road with pull-ins under cottonwoods, campers/trailers parked at several, running ~400 m from the highway turn-off to a large turnaround lot. The Dyrt 2021-09: 'We have a pick up with a 22 foot trailer and fit perfect ... Surprisingly level spots'. -> real drive-in FS campground; the posted 22-ft spur passes (AWH 2026-10-20). Horse rule: the corrals are at the trailhead (FS), which imagery places on its own spur ~130 m beyond the last pad, with a second trailer lot ~250 m beyond; no corrals or stock at the sites -> separate trailhead beside a general campground (Trails End precedent), kept with a flag.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World_Imagery (rendered) at 44.46252,-109.62893 (500 m frame), 44.4636,-109.6278 and 44.4605,-109.6315 (260 m frames), 44.4622,-109.6302 (200 m) and a z19 stitch at 44.4638,-109.6287 (~160 m): the stream beside the campground is Elk Fork, ~15-25 m of water (creek-sized, not the North Fork Shoshone the FS text names); the pads sit on the east side of the camp road ~50-70 m from the creek behind a continuous band of cottonwood/willow; only the trailhead turnaround lot (not a campsite) comes within ~25 m, still through trees. A 2020 Dyrt reviewer had 'a site with the river right behind us', but no pad could be placed at the bank over open ground -> defaults down to not waterfront (no creek-view value exists).

fees.note: Single unit. Fee season not posted; earlier FS and press sources had no fee charged in the off-season (roughly October-April).

season.note: Fees, host and trash service run in summer; the campground stays open without services the rest of the year.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/shoshone/recreation/elk-fork-campground ('Site Open' on 2026-11-20, when neighbouring Wapiti and Big Game read 'Closed for the season'; 'Open 24 hours/day') + FS Shoshone Visitor Guide 2011 ('Open year-round') + Powell Tribune 2017-09-21 ('Elk Fork Campground is the only one open through the winter in the North Fork area') + The Dyrt 2021-10-01 ('Open year round. Services discontinued the end of September through May'), read 2026-11-20
flags: HORSE RULE (the lead's question): the FS says 'Corrals are provided at the trailhead' and 'Horse corrals and trailer parking are available'; Natural Atlas: 'Horse corrals exist at the back of the campground, near the Elk Fork Trailhead'; Powell Tribune 2017: 'The campground has facilities for extended stays for horses, with several permanent corrals provided'; The Dyrt 2021: 'a large lot in the back if you need to turn around. Space for horse trailers.' Imagery: the turnaround lot adjoins the last pad (~40 m), the corral row sits on the trailhead spur ~130 m beyond the last pad, and a second lot (two long stock trailers parked) ~280 m beyond. No FS statement that stock is barred from the sites or confined to the trailhead; Outdoorithm's 'horses are not permitted in the campground' was seen only as a search snippet (the site answers with a Vercel bot checkpoint - refused, not retried). Kept on the Trails End precedent (corrals apart, none at the sites); if the reviewer reads 'extended stays for horses' as horse campers using the general sites, this becomes a skip ('horse rule').
RIG FIT: FS 'Maximum spur 22 feet' passes under AWH 2026-10-20 (22-ft limit passes); campers call the sites 'very small' with 'not a lot of room to maneuver' (Dyrt 2021). Tight for a 23-ft rig.
PIN moved from the FS point 44.46252,-109.62893 (open hillside ~60 m east of the sites) to the middle of the camping strip, 44.4632,-109.6290.
NOT A DUPLICATE: Wapiti Campground (6511) is ~0.5 km NE, a separate FS facility on its own road (rec.gov 234606) with its own FS page; Big Game (13705) is 1.8 km E.
PHONE: the Elk Fork page has no district contact block (only the Supervisor's Office, 307-527-6241); wrote the Wapiti Ranger District number from the sister Wapiti and Big Game pages.
FS text says the sites are 'along the Shoshone River'; they are on Elk Fork creek, a tributary of the North Fork.
Hard-sided-only and food-storage rules for the North Fork corridor appear in Campflare's copy of the FS alert; not written (not read from the FS order itself).
